papers.verified_title: Cross-Family Universality of Behavioral Axes via Anchor-Projected Representations
papers.id_resolution_note: RESOLVES EXACTLY. abs page returns the claimed title and both claimed authors. Submitted 11 May 2026, cs.AI, v1 only.
papers.transferred_object: DIRECTION (primary), which is then USED two ways. The object carried across families is a single unit vector c_a in R^N, the 'canonical direction' for behavioural axis a, living in the Anchor Coordinate Space (ACS) where N = size of the anchor pool. On a held-out target it is materialised either (a) as a CLASSIFIER input -- the target's prompt activations are projected into ACS and scored by a logistic-regression probe TRAINED ON SOURCE-MODEL ACS VECTORS, or by the training-free signed cosine s_a(x) = <pi^pt_{m_u}(a_{m_u}(x;L_{m_u})), c_a>; or (b) as an INTERVENTION -- back-projected into the target's native hidden space via v_recon = A-hat_{m_u}^T c_a and added to the residual stream. It is NOT a metric->behaviour MAPPING: nothing that predicts a held-out model's behavioural safety LEVEL is transferred. The per-prompt score discriminates axis-positive from axis-negative PROMPTS, not safe from unsafe MODELS.
papers.donor_requirement: Source (donor) models supply axis-labelled contrastive data: 'For each axis, we use 100 positive-negative pairs to extract directions on source models and 100 disjoint pairs for evaluation.' Default source set = 4 models (Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct, Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct, Phi-4, gemma-2-9b-it) with Mistral-7B-Instruct-v0.3 as the unseen target; 5-rotation holds each out once. The anchor pool is PROMPTS (N=300 sampled from 15 HELM scenarios, 20 per scenario, seed 42, 10-300 chars, deduplicated), but it must be converted into ACTIVATIONS SEPARATELY PER MODEL -- 'For each model m, the anchor pool Z induces an activation matrix A_m in R^{N x d_m}'. So THE SAME PROMPTS ARE RUN THROUGH EVERY MODEL INCLUDING THE TARGET. Sensitivity: source count can fall to N=1 (Llama-only 0.799 Multi-CLS / 0.938 Binary, Qwen-only 0.799/0.951, Gemma-only collapses to 0.472) and 2 sources already give 0.875/0.954 (L+Q); anchor count can fall to k=5 per scenario (N_anchor=75) at 0.832/0.952.
papers.fit_procedure: NO Procrustes, NO CCA, NO regression, NO SVD of an anchor-response matrix, and NO learned parameters. The projection is a FIXED linear map defined directly by the (mean-centred, row-L2-normalised) anchor activation matrix -- a cosine-similarity fingerprint. Verbatim equations: Eq.(1) a_m(x;L_m) in R^{d_m} is 'the final-token residual-stream activation at a fixed layer L_m'. Anchor matrix: 'A_m[i] = a_m(z_i;L_m),  mu_m = (1/N) sum_{i=1}^N A_m[i],  A-hat_m[i] = norm(A_m[i] - mu_m).' Eq.(2) point projection: 'pi_m^pt(h) = A-hat_m . norm(h - mu_m) in R^N.' Directional projection: 'pi_m^dir(v) = A-hat_m . norm(v).' Eq.(3) native axis direction: 'v_a^(m) = (1/|P_a|) sum_{x in P_a} a_m(x;L_m) - (1/|N_a|) sum_{x in N_a} a_m(x;L_m).' Eq.(4) canonical direction: 'c_a = (1/|S|) sum_{m in S} u-tilde_a^(m) in R^N.' Eq.(5) reconstruction: 'v_{a,recon}^{(m_u)} = A-hat_{m_u}^T c_a in R^{d_{m_u}}.' The paper is explicit that Eq.(5) is not an inverse: 'This operation is not an exact inverse of pi_{m_u}^pt. It is a back-projection that expresses the ACS direction in the linear span of the unseen model's anchor activations.' The ONLY thing fitted from data is the downstream logistic-regression probe, and it is fitted on SOURCE ACS vectors (scikit-learn, C=1.0, max_iter=2000).
papers.target_side_supervision: SETTLED FROM THE TEXT: the target model DOES require forward passes on the anchor pool. Verbatim, Sec 3.4: 'For an unseen model m_u, we do not compute v_a^{(m_u)} from positive or negative axis examples. We only forward the fixed anchor pool Z through m_u and construct its anchor matrix A-hat_{m_u}.' Therefore 'without target-specific direction extraction' means OPERATIONALLY: (i) no axis-LABELLED positive/negative prompts on the target, (ii) no contrastive direction estimated in the target's own basis, (iii) no fine-tuning or weight update, (iv) no probe retraining on target data. It does NOT mean zero target computation. The stated policy: 'The key policy is that source models may use axis-labeled positive and negative examples to form c_a, while the unseen model uses only the fixed anchor pool for direction reconstruction. No axis-labeled prompts, direction extraction, or fine-tuning are used on the unseen model.' Cost quantified: default 300 target forward passes; Appendix D.1 shows 75 suffice ('Even the smallest pool k=5 (N_anchor=75) reaches 0.832 Multi-CLS / 0.952 Binary-CLS'), with the paper noting this 'makes ACS construction practical even for very large unseen models where forwarding 600 anchors is expensive.' Additional hidden target-side cost: a per-model layer index L_m must be chosen, and the stated rule uses cross-family intra-axis cosine similarity in ACS (see citation_defects).
papers.eval_protocol: Leave-one-out at the level of ONE MODEL PER FAMILY, so model-level and family-level coincide by construction: five families each represented by exactly one main model, 'a five-rotation evaluation in which each model is held out once'. Held-out targets: 5 (Llama, Qwen, Mistral, Phi, Gemma), of which the HEADLINE 0.83/0.95 covers only the FOUR-family LQMP block -- 'excluding Gemma, the trained probes achieve 0.83 mean ten-way accuracy and 0.95 mean binary AUROC.' Chance baselines: ten-way multi-class over 10 behavioural axes => 0.10 chance; binary AUROC => 0.50 chance. The paper does not print '0.10' but confirms the scale by calling Gemma's 0.16 ten-way 'near chance' ('its ten-way accuracy drops to 0.16, near chance') while its binary AUROC 0.74 is described as 'above random'. Evaluation is on held-out test prompts disjoint from the direction-estimation split: 'All detection evaluation uses held-out test prompts disjoint from the axis-direction estimation split.' Refusal OOD generalisation without retraining: 'On LQMP, the classifier obtains AUROC 0.81 on JailbreakBench and 0.96 on XSTest.' Steering evaluation is an alpha-sweep in {-5,-3,0,+3,+5} with behavioural scorers (LlamaGuard-3 for refusal).
papers.what_was_held_fixed: NOT the tokenizer -- families deliberately differ in tokenizer and hidden dimension (d_m = 4096/3584/4096/5120/3584 for L/Q/M/P/G), and each model uses its OWN chat template ('We use chat templates as defined by each model's tokenizer (apply_chat_template with add_generation_prompt=True)'). NOT a fixed layer INDEX -- only a layer-selection RULE (8-fraction depth grid {1/8..7/8}); the chosen indices differ: Llama 12 (3/8), Qwen 21 (6/8), Mistral 16 (4/8), Phi 20 (4/8), Gemma 26 (5/8). HELD FIXED: the anchor pool (identical 300 HELM prompts across all models, seed 42); the readout position (final-token residual stream); the behaviour definition (mean(pos) - mean(neg) over the same benchmark splits, 100 pairs per axis, same benchmarks per axis across models); precision (bfloat16), decoding (do_sample=False), and the normalisation pipeline. All five main models are DENSE and INSTRUCTION-TUNED and of comparable scale -- no MoE, no base models, no non-English axis.
papers.verbatim_quote: "For an unseen model m_u, we do not compute v_a^{(m_u)} from positive or negative axis examples. We only forward the fixed anchor pool Z through m_u and construct its anchor matrix A-hat_{m_u}." (Sec 3.4) | "Across the LQMP families, detection remains consistently strong: excluding Gemma, the trained probes achieve 0.83 mean ten-way accuracy and 0.95 mean binary AUROC." (Sec 6.2) | "Gemma systematically deviates from the LQMP cluster, with some axes becoming weakly aligned or even anti-aligned in ACS. We therefore treat Gemma as a systematic weaker member rather than evidence for unconditional universality." (Sec 5)

papers.verified_title: Universal Refusal Circuits Across LLMs: Cross-Model Transfer via Trajectory Replay and Concept-Basis Reconstruction
papers.id_resolution_note: RESOLVES EXACTLY. abs page returns the claimed title and author. Submitted 22 Jan 2026, last revised 25 Jan 2026 (v2), cs.CL. Keywords line reads 'LLM, Alignment, Refusal, Mechanistic Interpretability, ICML' -- venue not confirmed as accepted anywhere.
papers.transferred_object: INTERVENTION, unambiguously. The end product is a rank-one WEIGHT EDIT applied to the target's attention output-projection matrices along a mapped layer trajectory: 'W^(l) <- W^(l) - gamma (W^(l) r / ||r||_2^2) r^T' (Eq.1), applied 'to the output projection matrices of each transformer block, i.e., the attention output projection (O-proj). For MoE targets, edits apply to shared attention projections (experts are not directly edited).' The thing literally carried donor->target is a COEFFICIENT VECTOR w (a 'recipe') over 20 concept atoms, but w exists only to reconstruct an ablation direction in the target and then edit weights with it. NOT a readout, NOT a classifier, NOT a metric->behaviour mapping. Its direction of effect is anti-safety: it ATTENUATES refusal (dual-use acknowledged in the Impact Statement).
papers.donor_requirement: Full white-box donor access INCLUDING refusal supervision: 'Donor: We assume full access to the donor (including refusal probes) to extract the source circuit.' Donor supplies (a) the trajectory window, defined non-adaptively as 'all layers where donor refusal probe accuracy > 90%', and (b) the ridge-cleaned donor refusal direction r_D. Probe prompts: 300 harmful prompts sampled from JailbreakBench. Exactly ONE donor per transfer (donor->target pairs, not an averaged pool). The shared 'anchor pool' analogue is the Concept Atom Registry (CAR): 20 concepts x 50 positive + 50 antagonist prompts, i.e. PROMPTS that must be forward-passed through BOTH donor and target to build A_D^(l) and A_T^(l) ('each atom a_i^(l) is computed as the mean activation difference between concept-specific prompt sets and a matched neutral set, using the final token of the user prompt, consistent across donor/target').
papers.fit_procedure: A per-layer ridge ENCODE in the donor and a linear DECODE in the target, over a shared 20-atom concept basis, with DTW for layer correspondence -- not Procrustes, not CCA. Verbatim definition: 'Two models D (donor) and T (target) exhibit semantic universality if a donor refusal direction can be expressed as a stable mixture over concept atoms, and the same coefficients reconstruct a functionally equivalent refusal direction in the target: r_D^(l) ~= A_D^(l) w and r_T ...' (Definition, Semantic recipe invariance). Algorithm 1: '4. Encode: Solve w^(l) s.t. r_D ~= A_D w (Eq. 4). 5. Decode: Reconstruct r-tilde_T = A_T w (Eq. 5). 6. Guard: W_T = U Sigma V^T; r-tilde_{T,safe} = (I - V_{1:k} V_{1:k}^T) r-tilde_T (Eq. 6). 7. Replay: Update W_T <- W_T - gamma ...'. Layer alignment (Stage 1, Eq.3): 'A-hat^(l) = NormCols(A^(l) - A-bar^(l)), G^(l) = A-hat^(l)T A-hat^(l)' then 'We map donor layers l_D in L_D to target layers via Dynamic Time Warping (DTW) on the distance matrix M_ij'. Ridge residualisation of the raw direction (Appendix A.1): 'beta-hat^(l) = (A^(l)T A^(l) + lambda I)^{-1} A^(l)T r_dirty^(l)', 'r_clean^(l) = r_dirty^(l) - A^(l) beta-hat^(l)'. Guard rank: 'k = ceil(rho d_in)'.
papers.target_side_supervision: 'Without target-side refusal supervision' means NO HARMFUL OR REFUSAL-LABELLED DATA ON THE TARGET -- and nothing more. The target still pays a large computational and access bill. Verbatim: 'All target-side choices are made using only benign data: concept prompts for CAR construction and benign validation text for drift checks (no harmful/refusal-labeled data on target).' And: 'Target (B_0): Only benign/concept prompts are allowed. No refusal labels, harmful prompts, or refusal-specific supervision are used to fit r_T, tune gamma, or select layers in the target.' Target-side requirements settled from the text: (i) forward passes on the full CAR = 20 concepts x 100 prompts = ~1000 benign prompts, at EVERY probed layer, to build A_T^(l); (ii) benign WikiText forward passes for perplexity/KL drift ('We select rho by measuring benign perplexity drift on a small validation set (WikiText)'); (iii) an SVD of the target's weight matrices for the guard; (iv) a PER-TARGET tuned hyperparameter -- Table 1 knob audit lists 'Guard ratio rho | Per-target | Yes (benign drift)'; (v) direct weight access and weight modification. The paper concedes the last point: 'this method is strictly white-box. It requires direct access to model weights and internal activations for layer alignment and vector extraction.'
papers.eval_protocol: MODEL-PAIR level, not family level and not leave-one-family-out. 8 donor->target pairs: 2 Cross-Family (Qwen3-VL-2B -> Ministral-3-14B; Qwen3-VL-8B -> Ministral-3-3B), 2 Reverse (Ministral-3-3B -> Qwen3-VL-8B; Ministral-3-14B -> Qwen3-VL-2B), 2 IN-FAMILY CONTROLS (Qwen3-VL-2B -> Qwen3-VL-8B; Ministral-3-3B -> Ministral-3-14B), 2 architecture stress (Qwen3-VL-8B -> GPT-OSS-20B Dense->MoE; Qwen3-VL-8B -> GLM-4.6V Dense->Reasoning). Only TWO base families (Qwen, Mistral) generate the cross-family cells. NO AUROC anywhere and therefore NO 0.50 chance baseline; the endpoint is judge-scored Refusal Rate (fraction scored 0 by a frozen Llama-3-70B-Instruct judge, greedy decoding) plus Compliance Rate, GSM8K EM and MBPP Pass@1, with 95% bootstrap CIs. Headline numbers: refusal rate falls from base 0.98 to 0.02 +/- .01 (Qwen3-VL-2B -> Ministral-3-14B), 0.95 -> 0.14 +/- .02, 0.99 -> 0.05 +/- .01, 0.92 -> 0.01 +/- .00, 0.94 -> 0.08 +/- .02 (Dense->MoE), 0.97 -> 0.01 +/- .01 (Dense->Reasoning), with in-family controls 0.99 -> 0.00 and 0.98 -> 0.00. The chance/no-op analogues are the four negative controls on 4 anchor pairs: Random-direction (Delta Refusal -2.1 vs Ours -81.0), Wrong-map (permuted layer mapping), Unrelated-Concept (transfer a 'Math' recipe), No-Guard (rho=0).
papers.what_was_held_fixed: Fixed across donor and target: the 20-concept CAR and its 50 prompts per concept, the atom token position (final token of the user prompt, 'consistent across donor/target'), the ridge alpha, the DTW constraints, the edited modules (O-proj), and the global strength gamma = 2.0. NOT fixed: the guard ratio rho, which is tuned PER TARGET on benign drift. NOT held fixed and NOT matched: tokenizer family, hidden dimension, architecture (dense vs MoE vs reasoning-tuned), scale (2B to 20B), or modality (Qwen3-VL and GLM-4.6V are vision-language models). The behaviour definition is fixed as the 3-bucket judge rubric (0 Refusal / 1 Partial / 2 Compliance) over 300 JailbreakBench harmful prompts.
papers.verbatim_quote: "Operationally, we ask whether a refusal circuit extracted from a donor model can be transferred to a target model -- possibly of different architecture and training recipe -- such that an equivalent intervention attenuates refusal in the target, without using target-side refusal supervision." (Sec 1) | "All target-side choices are made using only benign data: concept prompts for CAR construction and benign validation text for drift checks (no harmful/refusal-labeled data on target)." (Sec 6) | "Finally, this method is strictly white-box. It requires direct access to model weights and internal activations for layer alignment and vector extraction." (Sec 11)

papers.verified_title: Detection Is Cheap, Routing Is Learned: Why Refusal-Based Alignment Evaluation Fails
papers.id_resolution_note: RESOLVES EXACTLY. abs page returns the claimed title and author. Submitted 18 Mar 2026, last revised 1 May 2026 (v3), cs.LG/cs.AI/cs.CL. Code and data at https://github.com/gregfrank/routing-is-learned.
papers.transferred_object: INTERVENTION, and specifically a RAW UNTRANSFORMED DIRECTION used as an ablation edit. The transferred item is one model's native political-sensitivity direction, applied verbatim into another model's residual stream with NO projection, NO shared coordinate space and NO alignment step of any kind. The underlying scientific object is a ROUTING MECHANISM -- 'the learned conditional process by which detected concepts are mapped to behavioral policies during generation' -- which the paper deliberately separates from DETECTION ('whether the model linearly encodes a concept in its hidden states'). Frank's own framing: 'We measure it [routing] through ablation effects, cross-lab geometry comparison, and cross-model direction transfer.'
papers.donor_requirement: None in the anchor/donor-pool sense. There is no donor set, no anchor pool, no prompt set shared for alignment purposes, and nothing is averaged over source models. A single source model (Qwen3-8B) contributes its own contrastive political direction, estimated from its own prompt pairs; the paper separately notes that stable direction estimates 'require 60-90+ prompt pairs for stability; 8-pair estimates can be qualitatively misleading.' The only compatibility requirement is a brute one -- matching hidden dimension.
papers.fit_procedure: NONE. This is the decisive methodological fact. No projection into any shared space is fitted, attempted, or discussed; the direction is dropped straight from one model into another and is only even possible when the two hidden sizes coincide. Verbatim: 'Qwen3-8B's political direction applied to GLM-4-9B shows cosine 0.004 with GLM's native direction. The transferred direction does not reduce GLM's refusal (baseline 5/48, transferred 4/48, within noise). DeepSeek and Phi have different hidden dimensions (3584 and 3072 vs. 4096), making direct transfer impossible.' The within-model machinery that IS fitted is a ridge classifier (lambda = 1.0, fixed) for probing, plus leave-one-category-out CV; none of it crosses models.
papers.target_side_supervision: Not applicable -- no adaptation to the target is performed, so the question of what the target is allowed to see does not arise. The target is simply edited with a foreign vector and generated from. Note the asymmetry with the other two papers: they both spend target-side compute to re-express the transferred object in the target's basis, and Frank spends none.
papers.eval_protocol: The CROSS-MODEL TRANSFER claim rests on ONE model pair (Qwen3-8B -> GLM-4-9B), evaluated behaviourally on 48 prompts: 'baseline 5/48, transferred 4/48, within noise', plus a geometric read-out of cosine 0.004 against GLM's native direction. This is NOT leave-one-family-out and NOT a transfer matrix. The paper's leave-one-out design operates on a different axis entirely: leave-one-CATEGORY-out cross-validation WITHIN a single model -- 'We use leave-one-category-out cross-validation (LOCO-CV) on the v1 corpus. The corpus contains 48 prompts across 6 CCP-sensitive categories ... For each of 6 folds, a ridge classifier (lambda=1.0, fixed) is trained on the 5 remaining categories and tested on the held-out category. Each fold trains on 40-46 samples and tests on 2-8 samples.' Reported LOCO-CV generalisation 87.5-100%. Broader scope: nine open-weight models from five labs probed, four ablated, plus a 46-model behavioural screen at n=32 prompts per condition. Chance/null baselines ARE central to the paper but on the DETECTION side: null controls (food-vs-technology) and permutation baselines 'can all reach 100%', which is the basis for the claim that probe accuracy is non-diagnostic.
papers.what_was_held_fixed: Same behavioural domain (CCP-sensitive political censorship, six categories: Tiananmen, Tibet, Xinjiang, Xi Jinping/CCP, Hong Kong, COVID, each with a matched control), same corpus, same probing recipe across models (~12 uniformly sampled layers per model, ridge lambda=1.0). NOT held fixed: hidden dimension, tokenizer, architecture, lab, or scale -- and the mismatch in hidden dimension is precisely what makes transfer literally impossible for two of the models. Layer choice for the reported probe is post-hoc: 'The "best layer" reported in Table 2 is the layer that maximizes mean cross-validation accuracy across folds. This is selected post-hoc from the CV results, not from the full-training-set accuracy, which is 100% at all layers and therefore uninformative.' Models tested: Qwen3-8B, Qwen2.5-7B, Qwen3.5-4B, Qwen3.5-9B (Alibaba), DeepSeek-R1-7B (DeepSeek), GLM-Z1-9B, GLM-4-9B (Zhipu), MiniCPM4.1-8B (OpenBMB), Phi-4-mini (Microsoft), with Phi-4 and Llama-3.2-3B as Western controls and Yi-1.5-9B additionally probed.
papers.verbatim_quote: "Cross-model transfer fails. Qwen3-8B's political direction applied to GLM-4-9B shows cosine 0.004 with GLM's native direction. The transferred direction does not reduce GLM's refusal (baseline 5/48, transferred 4/48, within noise). DeepSeek and Phi have different hidden dimensions (3584 and 3072 vs. 4096), making direct transfer impossible. Political directions are model-specific, not shared across architectures." (Sec 3.4) | "By routing we mean the learned conditional process by which detected concepts are mapped to behavioral policies during generation." (Sec 1) | "H3 (routing geometry varies across labs and does not transfer): supported by orthogonal political-safety directions in four of five models (bootstrap CIs spanning zero), corpus-dependent coupling in GLM, cross-model transfer failure at cosine 0.004, and the Yi case showing detection without routing." (Sec 4)

disagreement_adjudication: Yes -- Frank's negative result is about a different object than Kim & Han's positive one, and the hypothesis put to the text survives contact with it, with one correction. The correction first: Kim & Han's transferred object is not purely a readout axis. It is a single canonical DIRECTION c_a that they deploy BOTH as a readout (an ACS coordinate fed to a source-trained logistic probe, or the training-free signed cosine against c_a) AND as an intervention (back-projected via v_recon = A-hat^T c_a and injected into the held-out model's residual stream at strength alpha). So on the intervention leg their object is formally the same KIND of thing Frank tries to move, and a clean 'different object' verdict cannot rest on readout-vs-intervention alone. What it rests on instead is method and protocol, and there the two papers are not in contradiction at all -- they are a method and its own no-op control. Frank performs ZERO cross-model alignment: he takes Qwen3-8B's native political direction and drops it unmodified into GLM-4-9B, an operation only even expressible because both models happen to be 4096-dimensional, and which he reports as literally impossible for DeepSeek and Phi 'because [they] have different hidden dimensions (3584 and 3072 vs. 4096)'. That raw cross-basis copy is precisely the failure mode Kim & Han's entire contribution exists to repair, and it is what their own framing calls out: directions 'are defined in a target model's native hidden space and do not directly transfer across model families.' Frank's cosine 0.004 is therefore not evidence against anchor projection; it is a measurement of what happens when you do not project, and Kim & Han would predict a near-null cosine for exactly that operation. The two results also differ on every other controlled variable. Frank's transfer claim is n=1 model pair evaluated on 48 prompts (baseline 5/48 refusals vs transferred 4/48, 'within noise'); Kim & Han run a five-rotation leave-one-out over five families on held-out test prompts. Frank's object is a POLITICAL-CENSORSHIP routing direction in Chinese-origin models whose whole point is that it is distinct from and mostly orthogonal to the safety direction ('orthogonal political/safety representations in three labs (cosine ~0.05)'); Kim & Han's refusal axis is a WildJailbreak harmful-vs-benign contrast in English. Frank's leave-one-out is leave-one-CATEGORY-out WITHIN a model, never across families. And Frank's own scope statement concedes the limit: his H3 is that 'routing geometry varies across labs and does not transfer', a claim about the causal gating mechanism, which he explicitly distinguishes from detection, where he finds the opposite -- the Yi case 'detects political content (probes work) but has orthogonal political-safety geometry and zero behavioral censorship. Detection is present; routing was never installed.' Read together the two papers make one coherent claim, not two competing ones: the DETECTION/READOUT layer carries shared cross-family structure that an anchor projection can exploit, while the ROUTING layer that converts detection into behaviour is lab-specific and does not survive a raw cross-model copy. Cristofano sits on Frank's side of that divide as to object -- he also moves an intervention, a rank-one weight edit on O-proj matrices -- but reports success, and the reason is visible in the method: unlike Frank he DOES fit a cross-model correspondence (ridge encode of the donor direction onto a 20-atom concept basis, decode in the target, DTW layer alignment, weight-SVD guard). So the field's actual state is not 'contested about whether transfer works'; it is 'settled that naive basis-matched copying fails (Frank), and settled that a fitted cross-model re-expression works for at least some families (Kim & Han, Cristofano), with an explicit known failure family (Gemma).' The downstream hypothesis's assertion that cross-family transfer of internal safety readouts is an OPEN problem is not merely contested -- it is false as written, and must be rewritten as a scoping claim about WHAT is transferred and at what target-side cost.
differentiator_sentence: Kim & Han anchor in ACTIVATION space -- their shared coordinate system is a 300-prompt HELM anchor ACTIVATION matrix A-hat_m that every model including the held-out target must be forward-passed to construct, and the object they carry across families is a VECTOR (a donor-averaged canonical direction) that has to be re-expressed in each new model's basis -- whereas the proposed metric anchors in INPUT space, defining its dose axis by two fixed English sentences at the prompt, so it builds no cross-model coordinate space, uses no donor model, fits no projection, and carries across families only a SCALAR pair (ED50, Hill slope) plus a metric-to-behaviour mapping that is never re-expressed at all.
what_kim_han_already_buy: Honestly and without hedging, Kim & Han already own more than the downstream hypothesis concedes. (1) They already buy cross-family transfer of a REFUSAL readout with no axis-labelled data and no fine-tuning on the target: per-target refusal binary AUROC of 0.94 (Llama), 0.95 (Qwen), 0.97 (Mistral), 0.93 (Phi), aggregating to 0.95 +/- 0.02 on the LQMP block against a 0.50 chance baseline. (2) They already buy a leave-one-family-out ROTATION protocol -- 'a five-rotation evaluation in which each model is held out once' -- over five instruction-tuned families, which is structurally the same design as the downstream primary endpoint. (3) They already buy generalisation of the refusal readout to held-out benchmarks WITHOUT retraining: 'we evaluate the trained refusal classifier without retraining on JailbreakBench and XSTest. On LQMP, the classifier obtains AUROC 0.81 on JailbreakBench and 0.96 on XSTest.' That is the closest existing thing to a no-recalibration claim, even though the paper never uses the word. (4) They already buy the cheap-instrument property: only 75 target forward passes are needed, since 'Even the smallest pool k=5 (N_anchor=75) reaches 0.832 Multi-CLS / 0.952 Binary-CLS', and only two donor models are needed (L+Q gives 0.875/0.954). (5) They already buy the negative half of the story -- a documented family where the shared geometry breaks, with Gemma at +0.19 mean cosine to the LQMP cluster and 0.16 ten-way accuracy, 'near chance'. What they do NOT buy, and what remains genuinely unclaimed by this paper: there is no threshold, no slope, no dose axis, no ED50, no Hill fit, and no interpolation between a benign and a harmful anchor sentence; the word 'calibration' and the word 'recalibration' do not appear anywhere in the paper (verified by regex over the full HTML: 'No matches found for pattern: recalibrat|calibrat'); and, most importantly, their endpoint is PROMPT classification -- does this prompt lie on the refusal axis -- not BEHAVIOUR prediction. Their 0.95 AUROC separates axis-positive from axis-negative prompts inside one model; it never predicts a held-out model's behavioural safety level, and they report no model-level quantity that could be regressed against behaviour. The downstream contribution therefore survives, but only if it is stated as a claim about predicting MODEL-LEVEL behaviour from an input-anchored dose response, never as a claim that cross-family readout transfer is unsolved.
kim_han_baseline_justification: Decided from the text, against convenience. The text settles that Kim & Han do NOT need zero target-side computation -- Sec 3.4 is explicit that 'We only forward the fixed anchor pool Z through m_u and construct its anchor matrix A-hat_{m_u}' -- so the strongest version of the overlap (zero-cost transfer) is refuted. But that does not rescue the contribution, because the decisive question is not whether the target-side cost is zero, it is whether the cost is SMALL ENOUGH THAT THE TWO METHODS OCCUPY THE SAME OPERATING POINT, and Appendix D.1 settles that it is: 75 anchor forward passes already deliver 0.832 ten-way / 0.952 binary AUROC. A dose-axis metric that interpolates between two anchor sentences will itself spend forward passes on the target of the same order. So the downstream paper cannot differentiate on cost, cannot differentiate on the leave-one-family-out design (Kim & Han already run it over five families), and cannot differentiate on freedom from target-side labels (Kim & Han already have it). A reviewer will ask the obvious question -- 'does an anchor-projected probe, which needs no axis labels on the held-out family either, predict held-out behaviour just as well as your ED50 and slope?' -- and nothing in either paper currently answers it. Anchor projection must therefore be RUN, not cited. Concretely it should be run in its two cheapest forms on the downstream paper's own held-out families: the training-free signed cosine s_a(x) = <pi^pt(a(x)), c_a> and the source-trained logistic probe over ACS coordinates, both with the k=5 (N_anchor=75) pool so the compute budget is matched. One honest adaptation is required and should be disclosed rather than used as an excuse: Kim & Han emit a PER-PROMPT score, so to compete on a per-model endpoint their scores must be aggregated to a model-level statistic (e.g. mean score over the harmful set, or the AUROC separating harmful from benign) before being regressed against behavioural safety. That adaptation is cheap and fair, and refusing to make it would be exactly the kind of convenience this adjudication is meant to prevent. Two further conditions for a clean comparison: use the Appendix C uniform-fraction layer rule (f = 5/8, which 'matches uniform f=5/8 within 0.003 binary AUROC') rather than the BEST_LAYER dictionary, to avoid importing the layer-selection leak described in citation_defects; and include Gemma or a Gemma-like family in the held-out set, since excluding it is what turns their 5-family result into the headline 4-family 0.83/0.95.
cristofano_baseline_justification: Decided from the text. Four independent reasons, any one of which would be sufficient. (1) WRONG OBJECT AND WRONG SIGN. The method's output is a rank-one weight edit that REMOVES refusal ('W^(l) <- W^(l) - gamma (W^(l) r / ||r||_2^2) r^T', applied to O-proj matrices), with refusal rates driven from 0.92-0.99 down to 0.00-0.14. Running it as a baseline for a safety METRIC would mean measuring how effective an ablation attack is, not how well a cheap readout predicts behaviour; there is no score it emits that could be correlated with a held-out family's safety level. (2) WRONG PROTOCOL. The evaluation is 8 donor->target PAIRS drawn from only two base families, and two of the eight are IN-FAMILY controls (Qwen3-VL-2B -> Qwen3-VL-8B, Ministral-3-3B -> Ministral-3-14B). There is no leave-one-family-out rotation, no AUROC, and hence no 0.50 chance baseline to compare against the downstream endpoint. (3) INCOMPATIBLE COST AND ACCESS. The method is 'strictly white-box. It requires direct access to model weights and internal activations', and on the target alone it needs ~1000 benign CAR forward passes at every probed layer, a weight SVD, WikiText drift evaluation, and a PER-TARGET tuned guard ratio rho (Table 1: 'Guard ratio rho | Per-target | Yes (benign drift)'). That per-target tuning is itself a form of recalibration, which makes it a poor foil for a no-recalibration claim. (4) REPRODUCIBILITY BLOCKER. Two of the eight pairs terminate in models that cannot be obtained -- see citation_defects on the 'GPT-OSS-20B' naming. Cristofano belongs in RELATED WORK, where he is genuinely useful in two ways: as the second independent positive result on the contested side (so the 'open problem' framing cannot be rescued by dismissing Kim & Han as a single paper), and as a citable precedent for accounting target-side cost honestly -- his 'Information Budget B_0' and the knob-audit table are exactly the bookkeeping device the downstream paper should adopt when it claims its own metric needs no recalibration.

late_breaking_overlap.title: Calibration-Family Overfit: Why Trusted Sabotage Monitors Don't Transfer Across Lineages
late_breaking_overlap.what_it_claims: Makes the untrusted policy FAMILY the controlled axis, fits a monitor on family A's transcripts and applies it to family B, and decomposes cross-family AUROC into three components -- how obvious each family's sabotage is, how capable each monitor is, and the residual own-family advantage after both are removed, which it calls the interaction. Verbatim: 'On code-backdoor transcripts the interaction is positive and survives the dominant confounds: +0.172 (95% CI [+0.158, +0.185]) on four open-weight families on a strict leak-free basis, holding across an eight-family matrix spanning four frontier vendors, blatancy-matched controls, a trained transcript-reading monitor up to 34B parameters, and a second code benchmark.' The mechanism is geometric: 'each lineage's sabotage occupies a different scoring direction, and rotating the monitor's scoring direction toward the target lineage recovers most of the lost detection while a matched random rotation recovers nothing.' Operational consequence: 'At a 1% audit budget under defer-to-trusted, an off-lineage monitor catches 19% of attack attempts where an in-lineage monitor catches 41% at the same audit cost, a +21.7-point gap.' Prescription: 'Control evaluations should report cross-family transfer matrices: a single-pairing accuracy overstates the safety a monitor delivers against a lineage it was not calibrated on.' Comments field states 28 pages, 11 figures, and acceptance at COLM 2026 (string truncated in the fetched abs page).
late_breaking_overlap.does_it_threaten_the_contribution: PARTIAL -- it does not preempt the contribution but it raises the evidentiary bar substantially and must be cited.
late_breaking_overlap.how: It does not propose a calibration-free safety metric, does not use a dose axis, threshold or slope, and lives in the AI-control sabotage-monitoring domain rather than refusal/harmfulness -- so the downstream contribution is not scooped. But it is the most directly relevant methodological precedent found for the phrase 'without recalibration': it establishes, with a confidence interval and a leak-free basis, that cross-family degradation is REAL and that naive single-pairing numbers overstate transfer. Three concrete demands it places on the downstream paper. First, its three-way decomposition (family obviousness / instrument capability / own-family interaction) is exactly the confound structure a leave-one-family-out (ED50, slope) claim must rule out; reporting only 'held-out families are predicted well' without decomposing will look naive next to it. Second, it asks for a full cross-family TRANSFER MATRIX rather than an average over held-out folds. Third, its rotation experiment -- target-directed rotation recovers most of the lost detection, a matched random rotation recovers nothing -- supplies a ready-made positive/negative control pair the downstream paper can adopt cheaply and will be asked for if it does not. It also cuts usefully in the contribution's favour: it is independent evidence that instruments calibrated on one lineage do NOT transfer, which is the gap an input-anchored, calibration-free metric is meant to fill.

late_breaking_overlap.title: Refusal Reads Only a Slice of What the Model Knows: Harm-Keyed Routing and Its Exceptions Across Model Families
late_breaking_overlap.first_author: not captured (surname Richardson appears in the truncated author list)
late_breaking_overlap.what_it_claims: Separates what the refusal decision READS from what the model COMPREHENDS, across four open-weight models spanning three families. Verbatim: 'moral comprehension is native to pretraining: a low-rank moral subspace crystallizes during pretraining, and alignment rotates it once without rebuilding it. The refusal gate, in contrast, is a fresh post-training construction with only a weak pretraining precursor, written into a narrow control-token channel where the refusal decision is orthogonal to the moral-judgment decision.' Central causal result is single-model (OLMo-3), via 'a nested interchange rank sweep [that] patches successively larger slices of the moral subspace between matched requests and reads how much of refusal's response transfers: as the basis widens, moral judgment keeps reading more of it, while refusal levels off at the level of a single harm direction, and about three-quarters of refusal's causal input lies outside the moral subspace altogether.' Explicitly reports family heterogeneity: 'The picture is not uniform across families. Llama reads broad moral content; Qwen reads beyond the single harm cue but is unresolved at our sample size; GPT-OSS reads harm, and its refusals can be argued in either direction by its own reasoning trace.' 34 pages, 6 figures, 15 tables.
late_breaking_overlap.does_it_threaten_the_contribution: LOW as a novelty threat, MEDIUM as a construct-validity threat.
late_breaking_overlap.how: It reports no cheap transferable metric and no calibration-free cross-family endpoint, so it does not scoop the contribution. Its danger is to the CONSTRUCT the downstream metric measures. The proposal's dose axis is built by interpolating between a benign-object and a harmful-object sentence of identical syntax -- which is, in this paper's vocabulary, a harm-percept manipulation. If 'refusal levels off at the level of a single harm direction' and 'about three-quarters of refusal's causal input lies outside the moral subspace', then a harm-keyed dose axis may be measuring precisely the narrow slice refusal reads, which is good for predicting refusal and bad for any claim that the metric captures safety more broadly than a refusal rate does. Worse for the transfer endpoint, this paper reports that WHAT refusal reads differs by family (Llama broad, Qwen unresolved, GPT-OSS harm-keyed), which is a direct mechanistic reason a single anchored dose axis might not transfer uniformly -- and it names Qwen as unresolved at their sample size, so it cannot be cited as a clean negative either. The downstream paper should cite it for the construct and should expect to be asked whether its ED50 tracks the harm percept or the moral judgement.

late_breaking_overlap.title: Local Sparsity Enables Unsupervised LLM Safety Detection
late_breaking_overlap.first_author: Xin Chen (with Gil Kur and at least one further author)
late_breaking_overlap.what_it_claims: Recasts deployment-time safety detection as anomaly detection over safe data only, motivated by the fact that 'new attacks and harm categories regularly arise, not captured by models trained in such a supervised fashion.' Works in the SAE concept space under the linear representation hypothesis: 'In the LRH concept space, which is typically recovered via a sparse autoencoder (SAE), nearby points share a small common active support. Using this local sparsity insight, we propose a framework for locally masked SAE-based anomaly detection, supported by theoretical justifications.' Validated 'on various architectures and datasets, including both capability-testing datasets and safety-specific datasets.' Crucially it does NOT claim calibration-freedom: 'when we allow algorithms to use 1% out-of-distribution data for calibration, locally sparse methods achieve near-optimal performance, demonstrating their ability to capture meaningful safety information while using only 1-2% of SAE neurons for computation.' Submitted 17 Sep 2026.
late_breaking_overlap.how: It is label-free rather than calibration-free, and its headline configuration explicitly buys performance with 1% OOD calibration data -- the very recalibration step the downstream primary endpoint claims to avoid. It also requires a trained SAE per model, which is a far heavier per-family cost than either an anchor pool or two anchor sentences, and it reports no leave-one-family-out transfer. It belongs in related work as the unsupervised-detection alternative and as a useful contrast: it shows that even a label-free method currently reaches its best operating point only with per-deployment calibration, which sharpens why a calibration-free endpoint is worth claiming.

late_breaking_overlap.title: Distribution-Specific Curvature Control with Finite-Sample Guarantees for Open-Weight Safety
late_breaking_overlap.first_author: Domenic (surname truncated in fetched abs page)
late_breaking_overlap.what_it_claims: Proposes HarmAlign, a defence against harmful fine-tuning of open-weight models that 'applies function-preserving spectral deformation along a estimated contrastive activation subspace', deriving 'finite-sample bounds for the estimated subspace energy and the resulting local harmful-distribution curvature lower bound'. Blocks direct fine-tuning and three adaptive attacks 'within a fixed-architecture, finite-budget first-order threat model'. Under submission to AAAI 2027.
late_breaking_overlap.how: Surfaced by the 'model-agnostic safety score open weights' query but is a defence method, not a measurement instrument. It produces a certificate about curvature under fine-tuning, not a cheap readout of behavioural safety, and it explicitly scopes itself to a fixed architecture, so it makes no cross-family transfer claim at all. Listed here only to document that the query returned it and that it was adjudicated as non-overlapping.

late_breaking_overlap.title: Item Response Theory for AI Safety
late_breaking_overlap.first_author: Joshua Fonseca Rivera (with Neil Shah, David Demitri Africa, Konstantinos Voudouris; UK AI Security Institute)
late_breaking_overlap.what_it_claims: Surfaced by the 'model-agnostic safety score open weights' query. Applies item response theory to AI safety evaluation; the fetched header confirms title, the four authors and the Independent / UK AI Security Institute affiliations, and an abstract opening 'Language models differ...'. NOT dissected further in this job -- it was already flagged as an occupied lane in prior project notes, and this job's scope is the three named papers plus leave-one-family-out overlap.
late_breaking_overlap.does_it_threaten_the_contribution: NOT ADJUDICATED IN THIS JOB -- flagged for a dedicated pass.
late_breaking_overlap.how: IRT supplies exactly the two-parameter vocabulary the downstream proposal uses -- a difficulty/threshold parameter and a discrimination/slope parameter -- so the naming overlap with (ED50, Hill slope) is close enough that it must be adjudicated properly rather than assumed distinct. The distinguishing question a reviewer will ask, and which this job did not resolve from the text, is whether the IRT-for-safety fit is per-family (requiring recalibration on each new family's item responses) or genuinely transfers a fitted item-parameter set to a held-out family. Recorded here as an explicit unresolved item rather than dismissed.

citation_defects.defect: The brief's figure '+0.46%' for the steering effect is wrong by roughly two orders of magnitude AND is a different statistic than a reader will assume. The arXiv abs page renders the sentence as 'canonical steering induces refusal-rate shifts of up to +0.46% under distribution shift', but the HTML body renders the same sentence as 'refusal-rate shifts of up to Delta = +0.46', and Appendix B.2 Table 10 shows the underlying quantity is an ABSOLUTE refusal-rate change of 0.460 on XSTest, i.e. 46 percentage points, not 0.46 percent.
citation_defects.further_caveat: The Delta is the RANGE ACROSS THE FULL ALPHA SWEEP, not a shift from baseline. XSTest canonical reads alpha=-5: 0.540, alpha=-3: 0.530, alpha=0: 0.860, alpha=+3: 0.980, alpha=+5: 1.000, Delta=+0.460 -- so 0.460 = 1.000 - 0.540, spanning negative steering through positive steering. The baseline-to-max shift is only 0.860 -> 1.000 = +0.14. The native (target-own-direction) reference achieves Delta=+0.550 on the same split, i.e. BETTER than the canonical transfer, and the random-direction control achieves Delta=+0.020. Any citation must state which of these three numbers it means.
citation_defects.action: Never quote '+0.46%'. If quoting at all, quote 'Delta = +0.46 on XSTest across the alpha sweep, against +0.55 for the target's own native direction and +0.02 for a random direction'.

citation_defects.defect: The headline 0.83 / 0.95 is a FOUR-family aggregate that EXCLUDES Gemma, and must not be attributed to the five families the same sentence advertises. Verbatim: 'Across the LQMP families, detection remains consistently strong: excluding Gemma, the trained probes achieve 0.83 mean ten-way accuracy and 0.95 mean binary AUROC.' The fifth family fails: Gemma's ten-way accuracy 'drops to 0.16, near chance' and its mean binary AUROC is 0.74; its mean cosine to the LQMP cluster is +0.19 versus +0.79 within LQMP.
citation_defects.action: Cite as 'four of five families (LQMP), Gemma excluded', and report the Gemma failure in the same breath. The correct reading is that transfer succeeded for 4/5 held-out families and failed for 1/5.

citation_defects.defect: Layer-selection protocol tension amounting to a potential held-out leak in the headline configuration. Sec 4.2 states the per-model layer is chosen by 'choosing the layer that maximizes cross-family intra-axis cosine similarity in the anchor coordinate space (ACS)' -- a criterion that requires the held-out target's OWN native axis direction v_a^(m_u), which Sec 3.4 says is used 'only for analysis, never for training or transfer'. The selected indices genuinely differ per model (Llama 3/8, Qwen 6/8, Mistral 4/8, Phi 4/8, Gemma 5/8), so this is not a vacuous rule.
citation_defects.mitigation_in_paper: Appendix C Table 11 defuses it: a target-agnostic uniform fraction performs equivalently -- 'The per-model BEST_LAYER matches uniform f=5/8 within 0.003 binary AUROC', with f=5/8 giving 0.744 +/- 0.181 Multi-CLS and 0.907 +/- 0.076 Binary-CLS over the 5-family rotation, and the mid-layer plateau f in {4/8..7/8} all reaching paper-grade performance.
citation_defects.action: If Kim & Han is run as a baseline, use the uniform f=5/8 rule and cite the Appendix C number, not the BEST_LAYER dictionary, so the comparison is leak-free.

citation_defects.defect: The abstract advertises 'Our evaluation across 8 model pairs (including GPT-OSS-20B and GLM-4.6V)', which a reader will take to mean OpenAI's public gpt-oss-20b. Sec 8.1 retracts this in a footnote-style aside: 'Note: "GPT-OSS-20B" refers to an anonymized internal research model.' One of the eight pairs (Qwen3-VL-8B -> GPT-OSS-20B, the sole Dense->MoE cell) therefore terminates in a model nobody outside the author can obtain.
citation_defects.action: Never cite this paper as evidence about gpt-oss-20b. If the Dense->MoE claim is cited at all, state that the MoE target is an unnamed internal model.

citation_defects.defect: Family coverage is thinner than 'cross-model transfer across 8 model pairs' implies. Only TWO base families generate the cross-family cells (Qwen3-VL and Ministral-3); two of the eight pairs are explicitly labelled 'In-Fam' controls; and the two remaining targets are an anonymous MoE and GLM-4.6V. The Qwen3-VL and GLM-4.6V models are vision-language models, which is nowhere reconciled with the text-only refusal probes.
citation_defects.action: Do not cite '8 model pairs' as '8 families' or as a leave-one-family-out result.

citation_defects.defect: The brief describes Frank as covering 'nine open-weight Chinese-language models'. Two corrections from Sec 1.1. First, one of the nine is Phi-4-mini (Microsoft), which is not Chinese-origin -- the nine are Qwen3-8B, Qwen2.5-7B, Qwen3.5-4B, Qwen3.5-9B (Alibaba), DeepSeek-R1-7B (DeepSeek), GLM-Z1-9B, GLM-4-9B (Zhipu), MiniCPM4.1-8B (OpenBMB), Phi-4-mini (Microsoft), described by the paper as 'nine open-weight models from five labs'. Second, they are not 'Chinese-language' models; the subject is Chinese-ORIGIN models evaluated on CCP-sensitive political censorship.
citation_defects.action: Cite as 'nine open-weight models from five labs, eight of them Chinese-origin, evaluated on Chinese political censorship'.

citation_defects.defect: Citing Frank as a general negative on cross-family transfer would materially overstate his claim. His transfer evidence is ONE pair (Qwen3-8B -> GLM-4-9B) on 48 prompts, with no alignment method attempted, and two further models excluded from the test outright because their hidden dimensions do not match. His scoped claim is about ROUTING geometry, not about readouts: 'H3 (routing geometry varies across labs and does not transfer)'. He separately reports that DETECTION generalises (LOCO-CV 87.5-100%) and that one model, Yi, detects political content without any routing at all.
citation_defects.action: Cite Frank as 'raw cross-basis direction transfer of a routing direction fails (n=1 pair, cosine 0.004, 5/48 vs 4/48 refusals)', never as 'cross-family transfer of safety readouts fails'.

citation_defects.defect: The hypothesis asserts that cross-family transfer of internal safety readouts is an OPEN problem. Against the primary sources this is false, not merely contested: 2605.09875 reports 0.95 mean binary AUROC on held-out families with no axis-labelled target data and 0.81/0.96 OOD refusal AUROC without retraining; 2601.16034 reports successful cross-family transfer on 6 non-in-family pairs. The genuinely open questions are narrower and should replace the claim: (a) nobody transfers a metric-to-BEHAVIOUR mapping, only per-prompt scores or interventions; (b) nobody anchors in input space; (c) nobody reports a cross-family transfer matrix with the obviousness/capability/interaction decomposition that 2607.06596 demands.
citation_defects.action: Rewrite the openness claim as a scoping claim about the transferred OBJECT (scalar mapping vs vector) and the ANCHORING SPACE (input vs activation).

citation_defects.defect: The words 'calibration' and 'recalibration' do not occur anywhere in the paper. Verified by regex over the full HTML: pattern 'recalibrat|calibrat' returned 'No matches found'. Kim & Han therefore never claim, and must never be reported as claiming, a no-recalibration result.
citation_defects.action: When positioning against them, say they demonstrate transfer without target-side AXIS LABELS, which is not the same as without recalibration.

citation_defects.defect: The keyword line reads 'LLM, Alignment, Refusal, Mechanistic Interpretability, ICML'. The trailing 'ICML' is a keyword, not a confirmed acceptance; the arXiv abs page lists no journal reference or venue comment. Do not cite as an ICML paper.

unresolved: ABSENCE OF EVIDENCE, EXPLICITLY LABELLED AS SUCH: across ten queries I found NO 2026 paper reporting leave-one-family-out transfer of a cheap safety metric to BEHAVIOUR without recalibration. The nearest thing found is 2607.06596, which reports the OPPOSITE (cross-family monitors do NOT transfer without calibration) in the sabotage-monitoring domain. 2608.05086 Item Response Theory for AI Safety was surfaced but NOT dissected. It is the highest-priority remaining adjudication because IRT's two-parameter model (difficulty/threshold + discrimination/slope) is structurally the same parameterisation as (ED50, Hill slope). The specific question left open: does the IRT-for-safety fit require per-family recalibration of item parameters, or does it transfer a fitted item-parameter set to a held-out family? Until answered, the downstream paper cannot safely claim its threshold-plus-slope parameterisation is unoccupied.

Kim & Han's FIVE-family (LQMPG) aggregate ten-way accuracy and mean binary AUROC were not extracted as single numbers -- Table 2's LQMPG column was truncated in the fetched window. The per-axis LQMPG cells that were captured (e.g. refusal 0.92 +/- 0.04 MC / 0.92 +/- 0.06 BC, math 0.80 +/- 0.39 MC, factual 0.69 +/- 0.35 MC, sycophancy 0.79 +/- 0.37 MC, toxicity 0.70 +/- 0.36 MC) make clear the 5-family aggregate is substantially below 0.83 MC, but the exact aggregate should be read off Table 2 before being quoted.

Whether Kim & Han's ACS scores can be aggregated into a model-level statistic that correlates with behavioural safety is NOT addressed anywhere in their paper and was not resolvable from the text. This is the precise gap the downstream baseline comparison must fill, and it is an empirical question the downstream experiment has to answer itself rather than cite.

Cristofano's diagnostics (Sec 7: spectral agreement, geometric alignment and distortion, depth-wise semantic progression) were identified by section heading but their numeric thresholds were not extracted. If the downstream paper wants to claim his method needs per-pair compatibility screening -- a form of recalibration -- those thresholds are where the evidence would be.

Frank's github repo (https://github.com/gregfrank/routing-is-learned) was not opened. If the downstream paper wants to reuse his political-censorship corpus or reproduce the cosine-0.004 transfer test as a negative control, the repo contents should be checked first.
